findings.title: Second `self.downsize` definition silently replaces the width/height version and breaks existing callers
findings.body: The file now defines `self.downsize` twice: line 145 keeps the old signature `(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts = {})` and line 149 adds `(from, to, dimensions, opts = {})`. In Ruby the later definition wins, so the 5-argument form at line 145 is dead code. Any code that still calls the old signature (e.g. `ImageSizer.downsize(from, to, width, height, opts)`, scripts, or plugins that pass width and height) now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (5 for 3..4)` on every invocation, so whatever that path did (avatars/attachment/post image downsizing) stops working at runtime. The old arity should be preserved in a single method that accepts either a dimensions string or width+height (e.g. a splat/branch), with a test for both call forms.

findings.title: Downsize loop ignores failure and never verifies the result, so oversized images are stored silently
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize` returns false when ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (corrupt file, unsupported format, missing binaries), and the return value is discarded here. When it fails the temp file is unchanged, so the `while` condition stays true and the identical expensive conversion is executed up to 5 times. When the loop exits, there is no check that the file actually got under `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` (5 passes of 80% may be insufficient for a large image and a small limit), and nothing rejects the upload. The result is that `max_image_size_kb` is silently bypassed for images that cannot be reduced, and up to five image-conversion subprocesses are spent on the request/deferred job for nothing. Break out of the loop when `downsize` returns false and return an error to the user if the final size still exceeds the limit. The guard is also only extension based (`FileHelper.is_image?`), so a non-image file named `*.jpg` triggers the same five doomed conversions.

findings.title: In-place downsize destroys the original: animated GIFs lose their animation and JPEGs are re-encoded repeatedly
findings.body: `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, ...)` rewrites the upload's temp file in place, i.e. the only copy of the user's file is destructively modified. The non-animated instructions use `convert #{from}[0]`, which selects only the first frame, so with the default `allow_animated_thumbnails` disabled a large animated GIF is replaced by a single static frame and the animation is irrecoverably lost. Iterating the loop also re-encodes the same JPEG up to five times, compounding generation loss. Downsize into a separate temp file, never replace multi-frame GIFs when animation cannot be preserved, and only swap in the result when it is genuinely smaller.

findings.title: Percentage dimensions passed by the new caller are not valid for the gifsicle (`--resize-fit`) path
findings.body: The controller calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(from, to, "80%", allow_animation: ...)`. For animated GIFs with `allow_animated_thumbnails` enabled, `optimize` dispatches to `downsize_instructions_animated` -> `resize_instructions_animated`, which emits `gifsicle ... --resize-fit 80%`. `--resize-fit` expects a `WIDTHxHEIGHT` pair (or `--scale 0.8x0.8`), not a percentage, so gifsicle exits non-zero, `convert_with` returns false, the GIF is never shrunk, and (combined with the ignored return value above) the loop burns all five attempts and then stores the oversized file. Pass pixel dimensions for the animated path, or use `--scale`.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10MB, ignoring the configured site settings
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` is now hardcoded to `10 * 1024` instead of reading `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']`, and the 413 handler at line 246 similarly reports a fabricated 10240 KB maximum. Consequences: (1) admins can no longer constrain what the client lets users select; (2) the same 10MB cap is applied to attachments, which the new server-side downsize logic does not touch, so a multi-megabyte attachment passes client validation and is only rejected (by the still-configured server limit) after the whole body has been uploaded; (3) the displayed `max_size_kb` in error messages no longer matches the actual server/nginx limit. Read the site settings and only relax the cap for images that the server will downsize.

findings.title: API URL downloads now capped at a hardcoded 10MB instead of `max_image_size_kb`, ignoring configuration in both directions
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes, ...)` became `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)`. An API client can now make the server fetch and process up to 10MB from an arbitrary URL regardless of the admin's configured image limit (followed by up to five ImageMagick runs per request), which is a resource-amplification change not controlled by any setting. Conversely, if an admin configures `max_image_size_kb` above 10MB, API URL uploads that used to be accepted now fail: `FileHelper.download` returns nil (the `rescue nil`) and the following `tempfile.size` raises `NoMethodError`, returning a 500 instead of a meaningful validation error. The download cap should be derived from the configured limits, not a constant.

findings.title: Public `OptimizedImage.optimize` arity changed and `OptimizedImage.dimensions` removed without updating callers
findings.body: `self.optimize` changed from `(operation, from, to, width, height, opts)` to `(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts)`, and the public helper `self.dimensions(width, height)` was deleted. Only three files are touched by this PR, so any other caller (plugins, maintenance scripts, specs) that used either method with the old signature now fails with `ArgumentError`/`NoMethodError`. Either keep backwards-compatible signatures or grep and update every in-repo caller in the same change.

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic-downsize behaviour or the changed `downsize` signature
findings.body: The PR adds an untested upload path and an untested change to `OptimizedImage.downsize`, which is why the broken overload and the ignored-failure loop above were not caught. Add specs covering: uploading an image larger than `max_image_size_kb` results in a stored file at or below the limit; an image that cannot be downsized yields an error rather than a silently oversized upload; an animated GIF with `allow_animated_thumbnails` disabled/enabled; and `OptimizedImage.downsize` called both with a dimensions string and with width/height.
